newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian minister says road toll too high.
newsitem.headline: Austrian minister says road toll too high.

text.p: Austrian Economy Minister Johann Farnleitner gave ground to the European Union on Thursday when he ruled out higher toll charges on Alpine roads and said motorists were already paying too much to use the Brenner Pass.
The European Commission announced last month it was taking Austria to court over the level of tolls on the Brenner Pass in Tyrol. The route is a main artery between Germany and Italy.

"Austria is already facing legal action in the European Court of Justice over the Brenner route. We do not want to risk any further proceedings by raising tolls (elsewhere)," Farnleitner said in a statement.
The Commission has accused Austria of breaching EU legislation by doubling the Brenner night toll for trucks to 2,300 schillings ($215).

"The Brenner toll is too high. It bears no relation to the actual costs of maintaining the road and is purely an instrument to control traffic," the Austrian news agency APA quoted Farnleitner as saying.
APA said the economy minister blamed the Tyrol regional government for Austria's dispute with the EU. ($1=10.78 Schilling)
